caveats: The publication-disabled simulated-Actions build-core run and the independent native-local build-core run reproduced the snes9x_libretro.zip package, resolver metadata, both ABI artifacts, and both active-marker build logs byte for byte. Execution was local; both builds cloned the pinned source over the network, so no offline source cache is proven.

This is static build/package evidence only. ARM64 is build-identity-bound to ra64-universal-v1 and ARMHF to ra32-a30-v1. ARMHF requires GLIBCXX_3.4.32, above the observed non-enforcing Miyoo Mini fallback provider value GLIBCXX_3.4.24, so the Mini profile is ineligible; A30 is the eligible 32-bit consumer at the ABI screen. Provider inspection and target-runtime capture are absent, so every execution profile and device view remains provisional and ineligible pending a runtime smoke result.

Content, BIOS/firmware handling, controls, audio/video pacing, saves and state round trips, reset and unload behavior, frontend integration, compatibility, licensing review, and sustained performance remain target-runtime and human gates. Publication remains disabled regardless of local byte reproducibility.

The publication-disabled simulated-Actions build-core run and independent native-local build-core run reproduced both ABI artifacts, resolver metadata, and package byte for byte. The selected github-actions/simulated/local-docker and reproduction local/native/local-docker identities remain explicit; evidence records and build-log hashes differ because runner profile, timestamps, run paths, run IDs, and parallel make diagnostic placement are evidence-bearing fields.

The pristine source is commit 185488cd83aaf274752a742c94d45561cbecb7af, tree da7c15404a93174aa0972d8ec053471e6cef064d, with eight recursively pinned submodules. Commit-derived GIT_VERSION '-185488c' is bound to all 54 C++ compiles and excluded from all three C compiles per ABI; the exact 57-object link uses the C++ driver. Both binaries embed '1.63-185488c', while resolver metadata reports display version 1.61, so metadata version drift is retained as reviewed evidence rather than silently rewritten.

Each ABI emits exactly two reviewed upstream compiler warnings: memmap.cpp has an unused close result and libretro.cpp compares signed and unsigned loop bounds. The ARM64 signedness type is long unsigned int, while ARMHF uses unsigned int; ARMHF also emits the reviewed serial-LTO warning and note. Parallel make moves complete diagnostic blocks relative to compile commands, so raw log hashes differ, but the order-independent fail-closed proofs bind the exact warning multiset, compile and link commands and reject any missing, changed, or extra warning, error, fatal error, undefined reference, or dubious ownership message.

ARM64 requires the AArch64 loader, libc, libm, libstdc++, and libz, reaches GLIBC_2.29 and GLIBCXX_3.4.21, and records CXXABI_1.3.9. ARMHF is EABI5 hard-float, requires libc, libgcc_s, libm, libstdc++, and libz, reaches GLIBCXX_3.4.32 and records CXXABI_ARM_1.3.3. Dynamic C++ and zlib provider availability is not proven by static inspection; loader, rootfs, frontend, and target execution remain runtime gates.

Resolver metadata declares the Non-commercial license. Any public distribution or release remains a human legal and policy gate even though the local create-only release reproduces; source and license obligations must be reviewed before publication.

Resolver metadata declares smc/sfc/swc/fig/bs/st loading, deterministic savestates, software rendering, and optional BS-X.bin and STBIOS.bin firmware. Neither firmware is packaged. Firmware discovery, Satellaview and Sufami Turbo behavior, controllers, audio/video pacing, saves, core options, game compatibility, and sustained performance remain target-runtime gates using separately supplied lawful firmware where applicable.

The software-only Unix recipe produces one shared artifact per ABI/build profile and provides no basis for device-specific duplicate builds. ARM64 is build-identity-bound only to ra64-universal-v1, while ARMHF is bound only to ra32-a30-v1. The ARMHF GLIBCXX_3.4.32 requirement is an especially strong provider gate for other 32-bit profiles; provider, build-identity, frontend, firmware, and runtime capture are absent, so all device views remain ineligible.
